subject: Microbiology
vignette: A 14-month-old boy is brought in after 4 days of high fever up to 40.2 degrees C, during which he had a febrile seizure. Today the fever abruptly resolved and a diffuse blanching macular rash appeared, beginning on the trunk and spreading to the extremities. He is otherwise well appearing and the family has no travel history.
question: Which of the following best describes the virus responsible for this illness?

options.text: Rubella virus, causing postauricular lymphadenopathy and a rash spreading centrifugally
Human herpesvirus 8, transmitted by sexual contact and associated with violaceous plaques
Human herpesvirus 6, spread by saliva and causing roseola infantum in children under 2 years
Varicella-zoster virus, causing a vesicular rash in crops
Measles virus, causing Koplik spots and a rash beginning at the head and neck

explanation_correct: Roseola infantum (exanthem subitum) is caused by HHV-6, spread by saliva, and presents with several days of high fever that can cause seizures, followed by a diffuse macular rash that starts on the trunk and spreads to the extremities in children under 2 years old. The mnemonic is that roseola gives fever first and rosy rash later. HHV-7 is a less common cause of the same illness, and the disease is self-limited.

explanation_incorrect.A: Rubella causes postauricular lymphadenopathy and a fine maculopapular rash starting on the face, and it is a togavirus-like matonavirus rather than a herpesvirus.
explanation_incorrect.B: HHV-8 is sexually transmitted, causes Kaposi sarcoma with dark violaceous vascular plaques, and is not a cause of febrile exanthem in toddlers.
explanation_incorrect.D: Chickenpox produces a pruritic vesicular rash with lesions at several stages simultaneously, not a macular rash appearing after defervescence.
explanation_incorrect.E: Measles follows fever with cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, and Koplik spots, and the rash starts at the head and neck rather than on the trunk.

educationalObjective: HHV-6 (and less commonly HHV-7) causes roseola infantum: high fever for several days with possible seizures, then a macular rash as the fever breaks, in children under 2 years.
